result.summary: Independently re-verified BACKEND-DEV's REQ-029 implementation (QR check-in via `ci_` deep link) against docs/agents/design/REQ-029.md, section by section, and re-derived every acceptance criterion myself rather than trusting the backend-dev handoff's report. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-029.md in full, then apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's performQrCheckIn/decideQrCheckinOutcome/overrideAdmitAndCheckIn/decideOverrideOutcome line by line. All four match the design exactly: row-lock-then-decide-then-write skeleton identical to toggleCheckIn (REQ-028). The S4 stale-token recheck is genuinely implemented (registration.ts:1276-1281): the locked row's `qr_token` is compared against the scanned `qrToken` argument inside the FOR UPDATE transaction, and a mismatch (or missing row) is treated identically to 'unknown-token' -- this is a real re-read, not a reuse of the unlocked §2.1 lookup's snapshot. 2. Independently re-verified AC1 with my own fixture read: apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.db.test.ts's 'REQ-029 AC1' test seeds a plain (non-EventStaff) member, scans a real admitted attendee's token, and asserts exactly one audit_log row with action='checkin.refused', entity='registration' (not 'event'), entityId=the scanned registration's id, actorUserId=the scanner. I ran this test myself (see commands below) and additionally read eventStaffAuthorization.ts's buildCheckinRefusalAudit to confirm the entity/entityId selection is a structural table (registrationId undefined -> 'event'/eventId; provided -> 'registration'/registrationId), not a string literal that happens to pass this one test. 3. Independently re-verified AC2: read performQrCheckIn's 'already-checked-in' branch (registration.ts:1294-1304) directly -- it returns immediately with NO `tx.update(...)` call at all on this branch (confirmed by reading the function body, not just the test), so the repeat-scan path is a true early-return before any UPDATE statement, not a same-value UPDATE. The test's own assertion (checkedInAt.getTime() identical across both scans, audit_log count for 'registration.checkin' staying at exactly 1) corroborates this at the DB level. Ran this test myself against the real scratch Postgres. 4. Independently re-verified AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6 by reading each corresponding describe block in checkinQr.db.test.ts and cross-checking against the domain code's decision tables (decideQrCheckinOutcome §3.2, decideOverrideOutcome §4.1), then running the full test file myself. AC5 additionally confirmed structurally, not just by test absence-of-string: getRegistrationByQrTokenForCheckin's own SELECT clause (registration.ts:1084-1100) never lists profiles.phone/profiles.email as selected columns, so the success screen cannot leak them by construction. 5. Re-verified eventStaffAuthorization.ts's backward compatibility myself: read the diff directly (git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts) -- both buildCheckinRefusalAudit and requireEventStaffForEvent gain exactly one new, optional, TRAILING parameter (`registrationId?: string`); every existing call site (REQ-018/028's /checkin, toggle, page-turn handlers) is unmodified in this diff and therefore passes no argument for it, preserving today's exact 'event'/eventId behavior. Independently re-ran REQ-018/028's own test suites myself (not trusting BACKEND-DEV's '11/11' claim): `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.db.test.ts apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts` -> 3 files, 26 tests, all passed (my own run, real output, see commands). 6. Verified the organizer-override's capacity-bypass scoping myself: `registerForEvent` is not imported anywhere in checkinQr.ts or referenced by overrideAdmitAndCheckIn (confirmed by reading both files fully); overrideAdmitAndCheckIn writes admission='admitted' via a direct UPDATE with no seatsLeft/capacity read of any kind, matching decideOverrideOutcome's own table which has no capacity branch. Confirmed the override callback handler (checkinQr.ts:177) calls `requireOrganizerForChapter`, not `requireEventStaffForEvent`, for its own authorization. Ran the negative-case test myself ('a plain EventStaff volunteer (not organizer) tapping override is refused, no write') -- passed: registration stayed 'withdrawn', zero override_admit_checkin audit rows, answerCallbackQuery alert = catalog.checkinQr.overrideNotAuthorized. 7. Verified no domain logic leaked into handler bodies (decision 0004): read apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.ts in full -- it only sequences calls (lookup -> authorize -> decide-and-write via domain functions -> reply by outcome.kind) and contains no admission/capacity/token-currency logic of its own; every decision is delegated to domain/registration.ts's pure decide* functions or domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts / domain/eventAuthorization.ts's authorization functions. Also confirmed no `now()`/`current_timestamp` inside any time-dependent predicate: `new Date()` calls appear only in the handler (checkinQr.ts:80,97,183), each passed as an explicit parameter into the domain function's `evaluationTime`/`at` argument -- the domain functions themselves never call the DB clock, matching decisions/0006's boundary and every existing REQ-020/022/023/028 function's own convention in this file. 8. No design-system token/component concern: apps/bot has no visual/CSS surface (Telegram plain text + inline keyboard only), consistent with REQ-016/017/018/028's own precedent, restated in design §12. No schema/migration change in this diff (confirmed: `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts` is empty, and no new migration file appears in the diff), so SECURITY-REVIEWER's S13 migration-review gate does not apply here -- there is no migration to review. No new npm workspace, no build-output relocation, no workspace script rename in this diff -- the Docker-build re-verification step in my own role file does not apply; skipped on that basis, not silently. Scope: every changed file is named in docs/agents/design/REQ-029.md's own file list; no out-of-scope files touched. The one modification to a previously-reviewed file (eventStaffAuthorization.ts) is exactly the one flagged explicitly by the design itself (§5) as necessary for AC1, additive-only, and independently confirmed backward-compatible by my own test run above -- not scope creep. Commands run myself, real output, repo root: `npm run lint` -> exit 0. apps/web: 2 pre-existing unrelated -element warnings (Footer.tsx:11:15, Nav.tsx:10:11), 0 errors. apps/bot: 0 problems. `npm run build` -> exit 0. apps/web Next.js (Turbopack) build compiled successfully, TypeScript check finished, 4/4 static pages generated. apps/bot: tsc -p tsconfig.json produced no output (clean). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, full suite, no path filter) -> 28 files / 286 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.db.test.ts apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts` -> 3 files / 26 tests passed (my own independent re-run of REQ-018/028's suites plus the new REQ-029 suite). One MINOR issue BACKEND-DEV self-reported in its own handoff (design §2.1/§7 not specifying a chapter-timezone field or a {total} placeholder, resolved additively by adding eventChapterTimezone and interpolating only {name}/{company}/{checkedIn}) is a legitimate plumbing/formatting decision within Open Question 3's stated latitude, not a business-rule invention -- concur with BACKEND-DEV's resolution, no rework needed.
